title: From MJ7 to Unity Level Design. Pt2
author: Radiant_Dog1937
selftext: A continuation of my work from [From MJ7 to Unity Level Design. : r/aigamedev](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1l8ei38/from_mj7_to_unity_level_design/). One thing I did differently from the workflow outlined in the first post with this room is cropping specific objects in the initial image before prompting ChatGPT to isolate the object. This made the resulting image much more representative of the source image.

comments.author: Radiant_Dog1937
comments.body:
The protruding warp core also caused some issues; I worked around this by generating a in painted image without the core and used that when prompting GPT for the rear wall section. Then isolating the core as its own object.

https://preview.redd.it/9g2xnsttsk6f1.png?width=2912&format=png&auto=webp&s=4e46e8c189c367c9cbc41e1d55e9f7571ba5bca7

comments.author: mudasmudas
comments.body: Are those textures in the unity level made with AI too? They look kinda weird in some parts. Great look overall, at least for a picture like this. I think it would be way to noticeable while actually playing the game.

replies.author: Radiant_Dog1937
replies.body: that's a consequence of the decimate feature on blender. When going from the 500,000 polygons original to 10,000 this issue shows up. I'd probably need to reproject textures using another workflow, but it's what I have for now.

replies.author: _raydeStar
replies.body:
You can reduce poly count using hunyuan by the way. It's really nice. 

For a wall piece you could probably do 2500 polys and get away with it.

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body:
Realistically that wall, should take about 200 tops (I think I'm even being generous), which is something that needs to be solved in the work flow for AI model reduction.

But still, really good, OP.

replies.author: _raydeStar
replies.body: Yeah; I have a workflow on civitai that I use, it is a little complex to set up, but once you're going you can select faces, create higher res textures, etc.

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body:
Nice,

I'm currently looking into a workflow for 3D, but, I'm just not happy yet, I think it's a little too much work with the current AI tech we have, but the 2D to 3D objects had pretty good detail, which did impress me even though the topology was a bit meh.
